requirements.requirement: 15+ Sigma rules, each mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique ID
At least 20 techniques assessed and placed on the coverage matrix
Threat hunts completed, each with a documented hypothesis and outcome
Incident case reports completed, full lifecycle from detection to closure
Rules validated against real attack telemetry: 100% of submitted rules tested against actual log data, not assumed to work
False positive review documented: every rule includes a documented false-positive consideration
At least three log/telemetry source types from the datasets, with a data dictionary describing the fields and their detection meaning
Every rule documents the ATT&CK technique ID, the logic and field conditions, a severity rating with justification, and a false-positive discussion
At least 3 correlation-style rules that depend on a sequence or combination of events, not a single log line
Coverage matrix marking each technique Covered, Partially Covered or Not Covered, with the supporting rule ID referenced
Cover techniques across at least 4 different tactics
A technique must not be marked Covered merely because a rule carries a related ATT&CK tag; coverage must rest on tested detection logic and evidence
At least one hunt investigates an ATT&CK technique not already covered by an existing detection rule
Hunt conclusions classified Confirmed, Inconclusive or Ruled Out; a negative result is valid if supported by evidence and no hunt is forced positive
IOC register with indicator, type, source event, timestamp, context, ATT&CK relationship, confidence, external enrichment and operational use
Each case report includes timeline from raw log evidence, root cause, ATT&CK techniques, impact assessment and a justified closure classification
Confirm findings using corroborating evidence from at least two sources where possible; every significant statement traces to evidence
Playbooks for at least 3 scenarios, each with trigger conditions, investigation, containment, eradication/recovery and stakeholder communications
For at least 3 rules, document a tuning pass: observed false-positive scenario, logic change, and the trade-off accepted
Executive summary translating technical findings into business-relevant language for a non-technical stakeholder
Reproducibility: every rule and hunt finding reproducible against the stated dataset by another analyst following the written method
Evidence-based claims: every conclusion cites the specific log evidence supporting it
Framework alignment: all detections and findings mapped to current specific ATT&CK technique IDs, not vague tactic-level labels
Version control: all rules and reports tracked in a version-controlled repository with meaningful commit history
Map each stage of the timeline to a MITRE ATT&CK technique and document a recommended containment/response approach referencing the relevant playbook
Final technical report integrating the project with stable IDs and filenames
Methodology document describing datasets used and how telemetry was obtained
Final presentation summarising coverage improvements and key findings
Each rule includes title, id, status, description, references, ATT&CK tags, logsource, selection/condition logic, falsepositives and level
Use real publicly documented security datasets; do not invent logs or incidents, and label any locally generated telemetry as such
Rules must be precise enough for a high-volume environment; do not maximise alert volume
All nine Section 12 deliverables complete: rule library, coverage matrix, hunt reports, incident reports, playbooks, IOC notes, executive summary, methodology, presentation
Four-week delivery structure with Week 1 data familiarization, Week 2 rule engineering, Week 3 hunting and incidents, Week 4 finalization, treated as checkpoints

Quality review against detection-rule quality, ATT&CK rigor, threat-hunting method, incident quality, playbook practicality, documentation and reproducibility, executive communication and independent judgement
Python 3.11+ with pandas and Jupyter, Sigma tooling, Git, ATT&CK Navigator reference, all in a reproducible pinned environment
Convert a subset of Sigma rules to a second query language to demonstrate backend portability
Build a small script-level rule-testing harness that runs Sigma rules against sample logs locally
Draft a purple-team exercise plan pairing detections with the attack techniques used to validate them
Determine OS, architecture, CPU, RAM, storage, Python versions, Git, IDE, PowerShell, virtualization, spreadsheet and presentation software, Jupyter, and establish the minimum required environment
Use a dedicated isolated Python virtual environment rather than modifying the global environment
Determine what components are missing and establish the minimum required environment; do not install software that is already correctly installed

Reusable notebooks for dataset profiling, detection validation, threat hunting and incident reconstruction, each documenting purpose, inputs, methodology, analysis, outputs and conclusions, with important results saved to durable artefacts

Lightweight local validation scripts checking required rule fields, unique IDs, ATT&CK tags, coverage-matrix rule references, validation records, false-positive documentation, incident evidence, playbook sections, and that every Covered technique references a validated rule
Professional repository structure with consistent filenames and unique IDs

limitations.text: Close the three evidence gaps T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder, T1110.003 Password Spraying and T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact.
limitations.effect: These three techniques stay Not Covered. They cannot be demonstrated with the two selected recordings, which contain no run-key write, no event 4625 authentication failure, and no labelled encryption sequence.
limitations.reason: Closing them would require locally generated telemetry. This host has no hypervisor, no VirtualBox or VMware, no working Docker daemon and no Hyper-V compute service, so no isolated Windows test VM can be created. The PRD and the engagement instruction both forbid running attack simulation on the user's daily-use environment, so the Atomic Red Team route is closed as well.
limitations.evidence: docs/environment-inventory.json records hypervisor_present and platforms_on_path as absent. coverage/matrix-v2.md records the minimum dataset each gap needs.
limitations.not_fabricated: No rule was written for these techniques. No telemetry was synthesised. They are reported as Not Covered with a stated visibility gap.

limitations.text: Measure the false-positive rate of every rule against a clean recording of normal business activity.
limitations.effect: 12 of 21 techniques are capped at Partially Covered rather than Covered. The coverage matrix is not overstated, and the cap is deliberate.
limitations.reason: Both selected recordings are adversary-emulation captures. They contain no baseline of ordinary activity. Three rules were measured against attributable benign background inside the captures, which is real evidence but not a clean-environment baseline.
limitations.evidence: evidence/tuning/benign-baseline.json states explicitly that it is not a separately collected clean baseline.
limitations.not_fabricated: No benign baseline was invented. The measured figures come from scripts/tune.py against real records.

limitations.text: Clear redistribution terms for the selected public datasets before external publication.
limitations.effect: The repository is not published externally. A redacted copy path exists but publication remains gated on a rights review.
limitations.reason: The pinned upstream files carry conflicting MIT and GPL-3.0 licence labels, which is a genuine unresolved ambiguity, not a formality.
limitations.not_fabricated: No licence claim was invented or assumed.
